page.layout: One printed page, one text column with margin notes at left and a few lines of catchword and signature below. Margin notes run down the left edge in fragments. Page number centred at top, no running head. Signature "H h" and catchword "Verùm" at foot.

main_text.p: [illegible, ~40 letters] cum famulis unâ mensâ assidentem, panem eundem comedere, vinumque idem bibere solitum, auctor est Plutarchus: Nec alius Assuero, saltem hoc tempore, animus, nihil voluit, quod ad epulum hoc apparatum fuerat, cuiquam negari, nihil à quoquam cohiberi. inde verf.7. vini regii mentio. ut quemadmodum de Cyro Xenophon institut. l.8. quæ sibi apponebantur, eadem planè suis concessisse; ita Assuerus quo ipse vino utebatur, idem planè, quodcunque & qualecunque id esset, convivis suis quibuscunque permitteret. Idque contrà planè quàm Persis Regibus olim in usu fuisse tradit, ab Athenæo l.4. laudatus, [illegible, ~12 letters], h.e. de conviviorum apparatu lib.2. Heraclides Cumanus: qui de convivis regiis, [illegible, ~10 letters] cum rege ipso potant, inquit; at non idem, quod ille, vinum. Denique sicut vino regio nemo prohibebatur, sed [illegible, ~8 letters], qodcunque poscere libebat, cuique concessum est: ita nec modus poscendi ullus definitus, sed [illegible, ~12 letters], sive, [illegible, ~6 letters], ut Joannes loquitur c.6.v.21. qantumcumque voluerat qisqe, poscere licebat: ita nec in hac etiam parte cohibitio erat ulla. neque enim hîc opus locúsve erat Spartani Regis cavtelæ, qi in convivio modimperator designatus pocillatori miscendi legem poscenti, hanc tulit,[illegible, ~20 letters] Si vini copia adesset, quantum qisqe poscceret; sin minùs, ex ego fingulis præberet. Plut. in Agesilai apophth. Potum, inqit historicus sacer, præbebant (ministri nimirum regii) scyphis aureis, qe subinde iterabant, vel mutabant; præbebant autem, ut vinum regni, i.e. regium, regiis usibus destinatum; ita plurimum, copiosum idem, juxta regis manum, i.e. pro regiâ facultate; prout tam amplis opibus instructum regem convivis suis suppeditare par erat: in eo maximè convivio, qo regni sui divitias splendorémque ostentare ambiebat. ut est versu 4. Sic omnino [illegible, ~6 letters] dici verè poterat; cum qi ullâ in parte cohiberet, planè nullus esset; sed unicuique pro libitu suo, qodcunque, qandocunque, quantumcunque poscperet, à ministris qibusqe porrigeretur: qem ego verborum istorum sensum, nec ambiguus id, avtumo genuinum.

page.notes: Greek passages in the first lines and the Greek words in the body (e.g. the Greek after "cum famulis", "Cumanus", "Denique", and "Potum") are only partly legible at this scan resolution and are marked illegible where I could not read them letter by letter. The left-margin notes are cropped fragments and mostly unreadable; I have marked them illegible rather than guess. The text "[illegible]" in the margin notes stands for such fragments. The Greek heading line at the top and the Hebrew-like abbreviation "ꝑ" near "dici" are doubtful.
